jobs.promptText:
Create a clear silent 8-second ANATOMICAL 3D instructional demonstration of Barbell Squat from the supplied exact reviewed starting image. Use its original gray/silver striated skin-intact mannequin, dark gray shorts, gray equipment, white studio and approved anatomical accent choices.

Start STANDING, matching the reviewed initial image. This delivery is a natural standing-start repetition, not a bottom-to-standing demonstration.
0–1 seconds: hold standing with the bar stable across the upper back and whole feet planted.
1–3.5 seconds: brace and bend the hips and knees together into a clearly readable COMFORTABLE SQUAT DEPTH. Show meaningful hip and knee flexion, with hips descending toward knee height as far as the mannequin can maintain coherent trunk/pelvic alignment and full-foot support. Avoid a shallow barely-bent pulse. Do not force extreme depth, heel lift, joint collapse or a numerical universal depth target. Keep the bar supported at the same upper-back location.
3.5–4.5 seconds: brief controlled readable depth position. Both heels and forefeet remain planted, knees track naturally with the feet, and the trunk stays long/braced.
4.5–7 seconds: press through the whole feet and extend hips and knees smoothly to the original standing posture.
7–8 seconds: hold fully standing without a second dip. Keep the bar, rack and plate geometry stable; no contact with the rack during the repetition.

Keep the camera completely fixed with no cuts, zoom, reframing or body rotation to display a different angle. Preserve the approved first image's anatomy, equipment, clothing, colors, lighting and full movement envelope. Orange, if specified in the start image, is a stable anatomical material region attached to the same skin surface: it deforms naturally with that body region, stays the same hue/intensity, and never slides, floats, spreads or pulses. Do not add colors to muscles that were gray. The accent identifies illustrative primary muscle involvement, not measured activation intensity. Show exactly one real controlled movement cycle. No extra repetitions, partial pulses, end-of-clip new motion, speech, music, sound effects or audio. Produce the actual return phase; no reversed footage or boomerang. Keep a readable still finish. Timing is a requested production guide; the operator must inspect the actual output before choosing any original-speed trim.

Keep the shorts dark gray; never color through clothing or turn shorts into transparent skin. Keep glutes, calves, knees, hamstrings, torso and arms gray. Surface color remains attached to the front-thigh volumes during bending.

jobs.name: Barbell Deadlift
jobs.promptText:
Create one precise instructional ANATOMICAL 3D starting-position still of Barbell Deadlift.

ANATOMICAL 3D VISUAL STANDARD. Create one original, realistically proportioned adult athletic mannequin with a neutral gray/silver skin-intact surface, carefully modeled superficial muscle contours and fine restrained surface striations. It is a clean medical-style 3D illustration, not an exposed dissection: no peeled skin, open tissue, skeleton, blood or exaggerated bodybuilding proportions. Use a simple neutral face, short neutral hair, dark gray fitted training shorts, plain gray low-profile training shoes, and gray equipment. Keep the torso and arms uncovered. Plain white seamless studio, soft diffuse light, gentle grounded contact shadows, quiet matte materials with restrained highlights. Preserve the same anatomy, shorts, lighting and material language throughout this comparison. This is an original SpotBot mannequin; reproduce the reference's broad visual language, not its exact character or exercise. No brand marks, text, arrows, floating dots, tracing lines, loose markers or ornamental overlays.

PRIMARY MUSCLE ACCENT. NO ORANGE ACCENT IN THIS EXERCISE. The catalog primary group is the glutes, which are covered by the required dark gray shorts. Keep all exposed skin and equipment gray, keep shorts opaque dark gray, and do not color the shorts or substitute hamstrings/lower back as the primary. Accompanying Form text will identify the primary group; visual accuracy takes priority over always showing an orange area.

CAMERA. Fixed near-side camera with a small front offset at hip height; show near-leg/bar relation and both grounded plate rims where naturally visible.

EQUIPMENT AND FLOOR CONTACT FIRST. Place one ordinary gray barbell on a flat floor, with full-size approximately 45 cm-diameter plates at both ends. BOTH bottom rims contact the same floor plane, with coherent contact shadows. The bar shaft passes through their centers at ordinary mid-shin height, approximately 22.5 cm above the floor relative to the realistically proportioned adult. No floating plate, gap below a rim, miniature plates, blocks or platforms.

NORMAL CONVENTIONAL FLOOR START. The mannequin stands with feet flat about hip width, bar shaft over the middle of the feet and close to the shins. Hinge the hips back and bend the knees to reach DOWN to the fixed grounded bar. Both hands close around the shaft in a symmetric overhand grip just outside the legs; arms stay straight. Hips are above knees, shoulders slightly ahead of the shaft, trunk long/braced and inclined from the hips, head follows the spine. This is the exact ready-to-lift floor setup before the plates leave the floor. Do not raise the bar to meet a standing figure. It is not a Romanian deadlift start holding the bar at the knees, a row or a deep squat.

COMPOSITION. Use the fixed near-side portrait camera. Preserve the complete floor-contact geometry, shoes, knees, hands and bar-to-shin relation. Reserve headroom for the SAME adult to stand fully upright later without reframing; do not straighten the starting body to fill that space. Include both full plate rims where perspective permits and allow natural far-side overlap. No rack, bench, extra plates, decorative equipment or duplicated limbs.

This still will anchor a single continuous exercise clip. Pose correctness, real equipment contacts and the reserved movement path take priority over decoration. Do not add a second view, pose inset, generated label or motion blur.

4.5–7 seconds: perform the REAL CONTROLLED LOWERING: hinge hips back, let the bar travel close down the thighs, then bend the knees as the bar passes them, returning both plate rims gently to the original floor plane. Do not drop, bounce, teleport or reverse footage.
7–8 seconds: hold the same floor-grip start with plates grounded. One complete lift and return only. Keep all skin gray and shorts dark gray; no orange patches appear during the movement.
